title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: Context: this sheet sits in Grothendieck's 1965 notes on a Galois theory of motives. The neighbouring pages are unrelated: they are a Bourbaki-style draft on analytic functions over valued fields. The page treats motives over a finite field F_p and their local avatars at each place. For each class xi_p in Sigma_p, which appears to be an isogeny or Weil-number class of motives over F_p, there is a pair (C(xi_p), T(xi_p)): a Tannakian-type category with fibre functor(s). This pair defines a gerbe G(xi_p) of groupoids over the l-adic and p-adic places. Grothendieck asks what happens 'at infinity', i.e. at the real place, and says the situation 'is not very nice yet'. His claims are these. (1) To each xi_p there is a canonical gerbe G(xi_p)_R over R (over Spec R, i.e. classified by Galois cohomology of Gal(C/R)). He does not know whether it has a description independent of the 'Deuring categories', that is, independent of the theory of elliptic curves. (2) For xi_p = the Deuring class (supersingular elliptic curves), this real gerbe is non-trivial. The reason is that End^0(E) = B_{p,infinity}, the quaternion algebra ramified exactly at p and infinity, and B tensor R = H. So C(xi_p)_infinity is equivalent to the category of vector spaces over the Hamilton quaternions H. In particular there is no R-valued fibre functor, only a C-valued one, and the obstruction is the class of H in Br(R) = Z/2. (3) Adding a polarization xi_infinity (Rosati involution, positivity) amounts to rigidifying the equivalence class of the gerbe up to a sign ambiguity. Using the reduced-norm functor V from rank-1 H-modules to the Picard category of real lines, one gets a functor 'canonical up to sign' from C(xi_p) to the category of real lines / Picard category C(R). This requires that the unitary 1-dimensional quaternionic vector spaces be 'well chosen!'. (4) Under this dictionary, the norm to 1-dimensional real vector spaces and the transposition correspond to the polarization and the Rosati transposition. Overall this is a sketch of the archimedean component of what later became the Langlands-Rapoport 'pseudo-motivic groupoid' and Milne's local gerbes for motives over finite fields. The archimedean fibre is non-neutral because supersingular quaternion algebras are ramified at infinity, and the real Weil group (normalizer of C* in H*) is the natural receptacle.
errors: The text is a rough sketch with heavy deletions. 'Canonical gerbe' over R is asserted without construction, and Grothendieck himself admits he cannot describe it independently of elliptic curves.

The category of right H-vector spaces is not by itself a tensor category over R. The real Tannakian content lives in the tensor category generated by h^1(E), whose real gerbe class is the class of H in Br(R). The identification 'C(xi_p)_infinity ≃ H-vector spaces' should be read as a statement about the rank-one / determinant level, not as an equivalence of tensor categories.
Sign ambiguity: the reduced-norm functor only gives a functor to real lines up to ±1. This is correctly flagged by Grothendieck ('au signe près').

ideas.what: Local gerbes at each place (l, p, infinity) attached to isogeny classes of motives over F_p
ideas.modern_name: local components of the pseudo-motivic groupoid / gerbes of motives over finite fields
ideas.usually_credited_to: Langlands-Rapoport (1987); Milne (Motives over finite fields, 1994); Saavedra Rivano for the gerbe formalism (1972)

ideas.what: Real gerbe of the supersingular (Deuring) class is non-neutral, since End^0 tensor R = H
ideas.modern_name: non-neutral archimedean fibre functor; Brauer class of B_{p,infinity} at infinity
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deuring for the endomorphism algebra (1941); Milne / Langlands-Rapoport for the gerbe statement

ideas.what: Polarization (Rosati involution) rigidifies the real gerbe up to sign; reduced norm gives a functor to the Picard category of R
ideas.modern_name: polarizations on Tannakian categories over R / Weil-number torus with positivity

missed.claim: Already in 1965 (or the late 1970s, given the cote dating), Grothendieck posits a canonical real gerbe G(xi_p)_R for every isogeny class of motives over F_p. He asks for a description independent of elliptic curves. This is essentially the archimedean part of the pseudo-motivic groupoid later built by Langlands-Rapoport and Milne.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an early, unpublished source for the adelic or local-gerbe picture of motives over finite fields. That picture is usually dated to Langlands-Rapoport (1987), which matters for the history of the Langlands-Rapoport conjecture.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an unpublished early sketch of local (including archimedean) gerbes for motives over finite fields, with the supersingular/quaternion example. It predates the standard credits (Saavedra, Langlands-Rapoport, Milne). It is fragmentary, however, and the mathematics itself is now standard.
transcription_corrections: The inserted phrase above line 3 reads roughly 'correspondant à la gerbe G(xi_p) des groupoïdes', replacing the struck 'les valeurs ... de'.
'édicté V de dim 1' is more likely '(droite V de dim 1)', an interlinear note about 1-dimensional quaternionic lines.
'V foncteur vers ordinaire vers cat. de Picard de R' is likely 'V foncteur norme ordinaire vers cat. de Picard de R'.
'Elle est, pour xi_p = classe de Deuring, qu'elle est non triviale' is likely '[Ce qui est sûr,] pour xi_p = classe de Deuring, c'est qu'elle est non triviale'.
The neighbouring pages are unrelated Bourbaki analytic-function drafts and give no context for this page.
